Latent transition analysis

Written by Mohammed Saqr and Sonsoles López-Pernas

Source: vignettes/articles/lta.Rmd
lta.Rmd

Latent transition analysis (LTA) estimates latent states at successive occasions and the probabilities of transitions between them. In the default model, profiles have a common measurement definition across occasions. With latent group classes, initial-state probabilities and transition matrices differ by class, representing heterogeneity in longitudinal patterns.

Data

course_engagement is simulated and has one row per course enrolment: 1,422 enrolments from 106 students. lta() needs three kinds of variables.

  • Group: student identifies whose occasions belong together.
  • Occasion order: sequence is the position of each course in the student’s history. Students can have different numbers of occasions.
  • Indicators: five activity measures (browse, lectures, forum_read, forum_post, attendance), each standardized within course, so 0 is the course average.
library(latents)

Fit

The lta() function requires indicators (vars), a group identifier (id), and occasion order (time). The arguments n_profiles and n_group_classes specify the latent structure; n_starts and seed control repeated estimation from reproducible starting values.

moves <- lta(course_engagement,
             vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post",
                      "attendance"),
             id = "student", time = "sequence",
             n_profiles = 3, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
moves
#> Latent transition model: 3 profiles, 2 group classes
#> 1422 observations in 106 groups, up to 15 occasions (unbalanced, observed grid)
#> Log likelihood: -8242.966906; 47 parameters; BIC (groups): 16705.1155
#> Converged: TRUE after 36 iterations; best of 3 starts
#> Smallest standardized Gaussian eigenvalue: 0.2092 (profiles, profile_1); Gaussian mass: 470.7; weight effective n: 589.7.
#> 
#> Class sizes   profile_1 33.1% (471)   profile_2 40.7% (579)   profile_3 26.2% (372)
#> Group classes group_class_1 30.0% (32)   group_class_2 70.0% (74)
#> 
#> Means
#>   indicator profile_1 profile_2 profile_3
#>      browse     0.396    -0.776     0.706
#>    lectures     0.189    -0.612     0.712
#>  forum_read     0.454    -0.888     0.807
#>  forum_post     0.345    -0.761     0.747
#>  attendance     0.254    -0.929     1.124
#> 
#> Variances and standard errors: get_results(x, "profiles").
#> Every other table: get_results(x, what = ), or get_results(x, "all").

The "starts" table reports the log likelihood reached by each start. Replication of the selected likelihood supports numerical stability but does not establish that the global maximum has been found.

get_results(moves, "starts")
#>   start log_likelihood converged iterations error
#> 1     1          -8243      TRUE         36  <NA>
#> 2     2          -8243      TRUE         48  <NA>
#> 3     3          -8243      TRUE         64  <NA>

Profiles

The profile plot displays estimated indicator means and the estimated share of occasions in each profile. For a transition model, plot() without an explicit view instead displays transition matrices.

plot_profiles(moves)

The profile heatmap expresses each mean in standard deviations from the indicator’s overall mean, facilitating comparison across indicators.

plot_profiles(moves, what = "heatmap")

Starting probabilities

The "initial" table reports initial profile probabilities (probability), profile prevalence across occasions (prevalence), and estimated group-class proportions (group_class_probability).

get_results(moves, "initial")
#>   group_class profile probability prevalence group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1    1.00e-10     0.0841                     0.3
#> 2           1       2    7.62e-01     0.8193                     0.3
#> 3           1       3    2.38e-01     0.0965                     0.3
#> 4           2       1    3.53e-01     0.4372                     0.7
#> 5           2       2    2.04e-01     0.2297                     0.7
#> 6           2       3    4.44e-01     0.3330                     0.7

Transitions

The "transitions" table reports the probability of moving from state from to state to at the next occasion. Probabilities sum to one within each origin state and group class. The column stable identifies transitions that retain the same state; expected_count reports the posterior expected transition count. A row with estimated = FALSE lacks information for estimating that transition distribution.

get_results(moves, "transitions")
#>    group_class from to probability expected_count stable estimated group_class_probability
#> 1            1    1  1      0.5202          17.54   TRUE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 2            1    1  2      0.3394          11.44  FALSE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 3            1    1  3      0.1405           4.74  FALSE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 4            1    2  1      0.0302           9.75  FALSE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 5            1    2  2      0.9386         303.22   TRUE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 6            1    2  3      0.0313          10.10  FALSE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 7            1    3  1      0.2221           8.71  FALSE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 8            1    3  2      0.2961          11.61  FALSE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 9            1    3  3      0.4818          18.90   TRUE      TRUE                     0.3
#> 10           2    1  1      0.5256         214.24   TRUE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 11           2    1  2      0.1141          46.50  FALSE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 12           2    1  3      0.3603         146.88  FALSE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 13           2    2  1      0.2099          43.69  FALSE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 14           2    2  2      0.6146         127.95   TRUE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 15           2    2  3      0.1756          36.55  FALSE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 16           2    3  1      0.4951         150.59  FALSE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 17           2    3  2      0.1277          38.85  FALSE      TRUE                     0.7
#> 18           2    3  3      0.3772         114.74   TRUE      TRUE                     0.7

The transition plot displays one matrix per group class, with current profiles in rows and next-occasion profiles in columns.

plot_transitions(moves)

Sequences

The sequence plot displays one row per group, coloured by the most probable profile at each occasion. These modal assignments summarize the fitted sequences but omit classification uncertainty.

plot_sequences(moves)

Classification

The "entropy" table reports relative entropy for occasions and groups. With more than one class, a value of 1 indicates certain posterior membership; 0 indicates equal posterior probabilities across classes for every case. Entropy summarizes classification separation under the fitted model.

get_results(moves, "entropy")
#>         level n_classes n_units entropy_sum relative_entropy
#> 1 individuals         3    1422       309.4            0.802
#> 2      groups         2     106        16.3            0.778

Diagnostic plots display per-case uncertainty within each profile (what = "entropy") and posterior probabilities of assigned profiles (what = "posteriors").

plot_diagnostics(moves, what = "entropy")

plot_diagnostics(moves, what = "posteriors")

Transition networks

The estimated transitions can be represented as networks. get_tna() returns a network pooled across group classes; get_group_tna() returns one network per class. Both functions produce tna objects that can be displayed with plot().

plot(get_tna(moves))

plot(get_group_tna(moves))

Beyond homogeneous transitions

Several extensions permit alternative specifications of temporal dependence and measurement:

  • transition_covariates lets covariates shift the transition probabilities: the log odds of moving to each other profile rather than staying. A covariate may change over occasions.
  • initial_covariates lets covariates shift the starting profile.
  • transitions = "occasion" estimates a separate transition matrix for each move.
  • measurement = "occasion" lets the profiles’ means and variances differ by occasion.
  • order = 2 makes the next profile depend on the two previous ones.
  • mover_stayer = TRUE adds a class of groups that never change profile.

enumerate_classes(..., time = "sequence") compares numbers of profiles and group classes, and bootstrap_lrt() tests a model against a nested one.

The following example examines whether previous_grade, which varies across courses, is associated with transition probabilities:

activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance")
homogeneous <- lta(course_engagement, activity, "student", n_profiles = 2,
                   time = "sequence", seed = 1)
grade <- lta(course_engagement, activity, "student", n_profiles = 2,
             time = "sequence", transition_covariates = "previous_grade",
             seed = 1)
get_results(grade, "transition_coefficients")
#>     group_class      from        to           term estimate standard_error statistic  p_value
#> 1 group_class_1 profile_1 profile_2    (Intercept)  -1.8398          0.118   -15.566 1.25e-54
#> 2 group_class_1 profile_1 profile_2 previous_grade   0.0338          0.121     0.280 7.79e-01
#> 3 group_class_1 profile_2 profile_1    (Intercept)  -1.4632          0.130   -11.256 2.17e-29
#> 4 group_class_1 profile_2 profile_1 previous_grade   0.0438          0.130     0.337 7.36e-01
#>   conf_low conf_high odds_ratio estimated
#> 1   -2.071    -1.608      0.159      TRUE
#> 2   -0.203     0.270      1.034      TRUE
#> 3   -1.718    -1.208      0.231      TRUE
#> 4   -0.211     0.298      1.045      TRUE

The estimated odds ratios are close to one, and the confidence intervals for the log-odds coefficients include zero. These results provide limited evidence of an association between previous grade and transitions in this example; they do not establish the absence of an association. A second-order model, in which the next profile depends on the two previous states, can also be compared with the first-order specification using BIC:

second <- lta(course_engagement, activity, "student", n_profiles = 2,
              time = "sequence", order = 2, seed = 1)
BIC(homogeneous, grade, second)
#>             df   BIC
#> homogeneous 23 16778
#> grade       25 16787
#> second      27 16786

For these data, BIC is lower for the homogeneous first-order model than for either extension. Extended models provide transition and initial-state logit coefficients, with Wald standard errors when supported by the fitted model, and occasion-specific probability summaries.

Assumptions

  • By default the next profile depends only on the current profile and the group class, and transition probabilities are the same at every occasion; the arguments above relax each of these.
  • Profiles have the same definition at every occasion unless measurement = "occasion".
  • Indicators are independent within a profile (the default diagonal covariance; covariance_model = "full" or a non-diagonal model relaxes it).
